title: The cube-root consistency threshold for Laplace mixture estimation
description:
For mixing laws on a fixed known interval, the ordinary exact Laplace NPMLE is uniformly Wasserstein-consistent in probability exactly when the known positive nondecreasing noise-scale sequence is o(n^(1/3)).

The proof separates the likelihood into category counts and the shape of reports that fall inside the support interval. The category likelihood gain is bounded in probability. A fixed Wasserstein separation creates a conditional shape difference of order the inverse scale, so the observed interior shape dominates once the sample size times the inverse scale cubed diverges. Two fixed laws with matching means give the converse testing bound.

Xiong, Ju and Rao posed the gap between their growing-scale upper and lower conditions. Earlier fixed-scale deconvolution estimates supply background. The new threshold concerns the full likelihood, including the tails, and covers any exact maximizing choice. Rational interval replay checks 528 interior ratios and 16 mass/tail bounds. The theorem gives uniform consistency in probability for known support and a known nondecreasing noise-scale sequence. Rates within the consistent regime and support-size bounds are outside its scope. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included.

Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof. OpenAI Codex reviewed the mathematics and revised the manuscript. GPT-6.2 Sol checked primary literature and prepared the worked example, executable checks, visual and release files. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author.
